derived_results.claim: For V(q;A)=sum A_i/q_i and positive simplex q,q0, uniform noninferiority V(q;A)<=V(q0;A) for every nonnegative A forces q=q0. Proof: choose A=e_i to obtain q_i>=q0_i for every i, then use equal sums. Therefore q0 is the only unconditional per-run backbone under unrestricted unseen next-run coefficients.

If next-run A may jump arbitrarily after an identical past history, no predictable nontrivial allocation can guarantee q0 noninferiority on the first changed run. Escape requires a pre-run/current-run signal, a drift/variation restriction, or weaker cumulative/time-average safety.

Replacing the generic 1.30 box cap with the exact simplex-box contrast against beta=0.5 improved recurring 40-stream mean ratio 0.86409->0.85467 and reduced p95 1.06568->1.05946 and worst 1.33432->1.30649. Abrupt mean was essentially flat/slightly worse 0.85173->0.85230 but p95 improved 0.96311->0.94091; gradual mean weakened 0.81236->0.81419. False upgrades remain because the box undercovers; conditional on true A lying in the box the false-upgrade rate is exactly zero by construction.

On 16 fresh streams/scenario, same-run completed scalar contrast measurement error normalized by range R had q95 about 0.0115/0.0120/0.0141 for abrupt/gradual/recurring. Pre-run center staleness had recurring q95 0.1030 and q99 0.1555; abrupt q99 0.1234 despite a small q95 because the change is rare. Temporal surprise dominates completed scalar measurement noise.

Even plugging the exact realized ||A-d||_1 into the deterministic R||A-d||_1/2 bridge certified only 23.0%/25.8%/38.7% of true-safe aggressive runs in abrupt/gradual/recurring stress. The statistical target should be the one-dimensional contrast error directly.

A high-fidelity synthetic normalized margin kappa=0.055, selected on 8 discovery streams/scenario to keep observed overall false upgrades below 1%, validated on 24 disjoint streams/scenario with overall false upgrade 0.00604 but mean beta only about 0.515/0.512/0.511. Weighted mean gain over fixed beta=0.5 was only about 0.12%, while recurring worst was 1.08797 vs fixed 1.07602. Without a pre-run drift feature, strong calibration collapses toward the backbone.

A fresh current-run uniform pilot can eliminate staleness in principle, but discarding a full-fidelity pilot is too expensive at total budget 768. A 16-per-generation pilot with beta=0.65 gave allocation-only mean 0.86553 and p95 1.01652 across 23 half-step positions before pilot cost; charging the 192-unit full cost makes mean total efficiency worse than uniform. The viable escape is a much cheaper low-fidelity pilot or a correctness-preserving way to reuse pilot samples.

engineering_update.scope: Reconstructed role-local two-state Feynman-Kac harness, exact allocation algebra, 40-stream closed-loop allocation validation, 16-stream scalar error diagnostics, 8-stream discovery plus 24-stream held-out margin validation, and exploratory pilot-cost screening. All numeric effects are model-specific.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The impossibility result concerns unrestricted per-run next-coefficient safety, not cumulative regret or structured drift.
Decision-specific robust allocation cannot fix an uncertainty set that misses the true current coefficient vector.
Same-run scalar diagnostics are accurate only after the run; without pre-run information they cannot protect the first unseen abrupt-change run.
The kappa margin uses synthetic post-hoc true A for discovery and is not an online theorem.
The discarded-pilot experiment is only a screening design and ignores fixed overhead; it does not rule out adaptive Neyman/sample-splitting schemes that reuse pilot data safely.
No theorem-clean one-step scalar contrast estimator under independent stratified multi-generation particle dependence was established.
No real-agent or AGI performance claim follows from the synthetic model.
frontier: Adopt the no-free-lunch boundary explicitly: q0 is the only unconditional per-run guarantee. Do not search for assumption-free next-run improvement from past-only diagnostics.
Use the exact robust contrast rule for conditional upgrades and orient uncertainty/calibration directly along c dot A, not the full 12-dimensional coefficient vector.

Separate completed-run scalar measurement error from temporal drift. Build a directional dataset with predicted/completed/true contrasts and regime-change flags, then test explicit variation-budget/window rules only under stated drift assumptions.

Explore pre-run/current-run information: cheap low-fidelity pilot, task/context covariate, or reusable sample-splitting. Prove estimator correctness before counting current-run pilot information toward the final result.
Continue theorem search for a scalar influence/contrast confidence object under independent stratified particle dependence; a full-vector theorem is no longer the priority.
exact_next_action: Keep beta=0.5 as the sole unconditional per-run backbone. In the synthetic harness, store the one-dimensional decision contrast and its range on every run, separately recording completed-measurement error and temporal staleness. Prespecify a scalar variation-budget/window rule and validate it only under the corresponding drift class; report first-change loss separately. In parallel design a two-stage sample-splitting experiment where a cheap or reusable current-run pilot estimates the scalar contrast before an independent production allocation. Include pilot cost, ensure the final estimator remains valid under the adaptive allocation, and compare against the history-only q0 and exact conditional robust-contrast controllers.
